Modeling ethnic differences via drug-predicted clearance from chemical structures.

The authors developed a machine-learning approach that predicts drug clearance directly from chemical structures and uses these predictions to flag the risk of ethnic differences in pharmacokinetics at early drug-discovery stages. This offers a complementary screening tool to physiologically based pharmacokinetic modeling when experimental data are limited.

Design, synthesis, and docking analysis of benzene sulfonamide-[1,4]benzoxazepine hybrids as acetylcholinesterase and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitors.

The authors synthesized a series of hybrid molecules combining benzene sulfonamide and [1,4]benzoxazepine scaffolds and tested them as inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), enzymes targeted in Alzheimer's disease. Several compounds showed micromolar dual inhibition, with compound 12j being the most potent BChE inhibitor (IC50 ~1 µM) and showing selectivity for BChE over AChE. Docking analysis was used to rationalize binding. This is early-stage medicinal chemistry work with in vitro data only.

Structure-function relationships in a square-planar Cu(ii) hybrid halometalate: experimental, DFT, molecular docking, optical, and biological studies.
